published_prior_art.cite: andrews2000boundary supplies general boundary-local asymptotics, but not this fixed-relevance leaky-IV Gaussian path.
watson2024bounding gives the p=2 endpoint formula and retained-resample coverage claim, but not a contact-local fourth-root or random retained-kernel law.

fangSantos2019directional gives a general ordinary-bootstrap criterion for directionally differentiable maps, but does not analyze the half-Hölder leaky-IV endpoint or endogenous feasibility retention.
chernozhukovNeweySantos2023constrained and chernozhukovChetverikovKato2013gaussian provide related constrained/bootstrap couplings, not this quadratic-score contact/interior loss transfer.
romanoShaikh2010identifiedSet provides general uniform identified-set coverage; no verified result gives this one-rule n^-1/4 contact and n^-1/2 interior directed-loss result for leaky IV.
hiranoPorter2012impossibility establishes nonregular-estimation impossibility, not a matched directed-Hausdorff lower rate on this leaky-IV experiment.

soundness_flags.label: def:totalized-plugin / def:multiplier-hull
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed every-sample procedures remain undefined when the sample instrument covariance block is singular, an event allowed by the stated law class; totalize the inverse (or specify a measurable fallback) before defining all endpoint and score objects.

soundness_flags.label: thm:adaptive-score-hull and thm:minimax-loss-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: C_n and the competing D_n may be empty, but d_arrow(A,B) is not defined for an empty first argument; define the loss convention or restrict the random-set class.

soundness_flags.label: thm:witness-membership-lan
soundness_flags.one_line: Membership in P_n^ct(C_delta) requires C_delta at least H_bar, and membership in P_W additionally requires explicit compatibility of K and the covariance/interiority constants; neither condition is stated.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3692–3695, Corollary 2.1 and Theorem 4; p. 3707, Appendix A.9
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary 2.1 gives the p=2 square-root endpoints; Theorem 4 resamples subject to bootstrap feasibility; Appendix A.9 calls the bounds differentiable functions of covariance moments and restricts attention to feasible resamples.
Under a Gaussian first-stage limit, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap consistency in the stated directional-differentiability framework.
The paper rules out locally asymptotically unbiased and alpha-quantile-unbiased estimation for nondifferentiable functionals, rather than giving a leaky-IV set-loss rate.
The paper constructs random sets covering identified sets, including uniform-in-P validity under conditions.
The paper obtains uniformly valid bootstrap critical values through approximation of a subset of a local parameter space in constrained conditional-moment models.
The paper gives Gaussian and Gaussian-multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional vector sums.
The numerical bootstrap is studied under fixed and drifting sequences, with applications including constrained estimators and partially identified-model test statistics.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 236 (2025), article 106245
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proximal bootstrap targets uniformly valid inference for root-n-consistent constrained optimization estimators near or away from a boundary.
The preprint develops local minimax lower-bound machinery for nonsmooth functionals and irregular statistical models.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make every finite-sample covariance-based object genuinely total by specifying a pseudoinverse, ridge rule, or explicit fallback on singular sample covariance blocks, then prove the fallback is asymptotically immaterial.
State the witness compatibility regime explicitly: C_delta >= H_bar, a distinct K-interiority constant, and numerical covariance-eigenvalue bounds satisfied by Sigma(a) uniformly on the path.

Add a worked finite-n Gaussian calculation comparing ordinary and retained bootstrap endpoint laws at h=0 and h>0; it will make the named-workflow diagnosis independently checkable before pursuing the uniform multiplier result.

recommended_next_step: Revise the sample-object totalization, random-set loss convention, and Gaussian-witness constant regime, then retain this field-grade contact-inference angle for Stage 0.
